question:
Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.
As global
P. electricity generation is expected to
Q. significantly to maintain its current share of the mix
R. double over the next three decades, nuclear power
S. generating capacity would need to expand
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. PRSQ.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The complete, meaningful sentence reads: "As global electricity generation is expected to double over the next three decades, nuclear power generating capacity would need to expand significantly to maintain its current share of the mix."

• Rule — Sentence rearrangement: always locate the part that grammatically completes the opening fragment first, then trace the subject that carries the rest of the sentence, and finally attach the part that logically closes the idea.

• The fragment "As global" needs a noun + verb to complete the subordinate clause, which comes from P ("electricity generation is expected to").

◦ P in turn needs an infinitive verb, supplied by R ("double over the next three decades, nuclear power") — giving "is expected to double" and introducing the new subject "nuclear power".

◦ S ("generating capacity would need to expand") completes the predicate of "nuclear power", forming "nuclear power generating capacity would need to expand".

◦ Q ("significantly to maintain its current share of the mix") logically closes the sentence, telling us how much the capacity must expand and for what purpose.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 (QSPR) is incorrect because it opens with "significantly to maintain..." right after "As global", which is grammatically broken and meaningless.

• Option 3 (PQSR) is incorrect because P is directly followed by Q, so "is expected to" is never given its verb "double", producing an incomplete clause.

• Option 4 (SQPR) is incorrect because it starts with "generating capacity would need to expand" immediately after "As global", which has no logical subject at that point.

NOTE

• In sentence-rearrangement questions, always check: (1) which part must open the sentence, (2) pronoun/possessive references (his, its, their) that must follow the noun they refer to, and (3) conjunctions/prepositions that signal continuity ("and", "but", "to", "over").

• Reading the assembled sentence aloud after selecting an option is the fastest way to catch a broken or illogical order.

question:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.
My father fixed the computer easily.
option_1: The computer was fixed by my father easily.
option_2: The computer is fixed by my father easily.
option_3: The computer was fix by my father easily.
option_4: The computer fixed by my father easily.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. The computer was fixed by my father easily.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The given sentence "My father fixed the computer easily" is in the Simple Past Tense, assertive, active voice.

• Rule — Simple Past Tense:
◦ Active: Subject + V2 + Object
◦ Passive: Object + was/were + V3 + by + Subject

• Applying the rule: the object "the computer" (singular) becomes the subject, so the auxiliary used is "was"; the verb "fixed" becomes the past participle "fixed" (V3 of "fix" is also "fixed"); and "my father" becomes the agent introduced by "by". The adverb "easily" stays at the end.
◦ Passive: The computer was fixed by my father easily.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 is incorrect because "is fixed" is a Present Tense passive form, but the original sentence is in the Past Tense.

• Option 3 is incorrect because "was fix" uses the base form "fix" instead of the required past participle "fixed" after the auxiliary "was".

• Option 4 is incorrect because it drops the auxiliary verb "was" altogether — "The computer fixed by my father" is not a grammatically complete passive construction.

NOTE

• Regular verbs like fix, walk, play have identical Past (V2) and Past Participle (V3) forms, which is why students often confuse active V2 with passive V3 — always check that an auxiliary (is/am/are/was/were/has/have/had been) precedes the V3 form in the passive.

• Adverbs of manner (easily, quickly, carefully) generally retain their position at the end of the clause when converting active to passive.

question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.
To take the veil
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. To become a nun.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "To take the veil" means to become a nun, i.e., to enter a convent and devote one's life to religious service. (नन (साध्वी) बनना)
◦ Example: After her fiance's death, she decided to take the veil and spent the rest of her life in the convent.

• The expression originates from the ceremonial veil worn by Christian nuns at the time they formally take their religious vows, symbolising their withdrawal from worldly life.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: To help someone — this is not related to the idiom; it describes plain assistance, not a religious commitment.

• Option 3: To take a responsibility — this describes accepting a duty or task, which is unrelated to the specific religious meaning of "to take the veil".

• Option 4: To show interest — this is a general expression of curiosity or attentiveness, not connected to becoming a nun.

NOTE

• Other religion-related idioms asked in SSC: "To take orders" (to become a priest), "To join the church" (to become a member of the clergy), and "To take the cowl" (to become a monk).

question: Choose the correctly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Emphatic.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "Emphatic" — expressing something forcibly and clearly; showing emphasis. (जोरदार/स्पष्ट)
◦ Example: The minister gave an emphatic denial of the corruption charges.

• Spelling key: EM + PHA + TIC. Note the "ph" (pronounced as "f") and the ending "-atic", not "-etic" or "-itic".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Gregareous" — incorrect; the correct spelling is "Gregarious" (sociable, fond of company).

• Option 3: "Liberanian" — incorrect; there is no such standard English word with this spelling (the word intended is likely "Librarian", spelt quite differently).

• Option 4: "Gangstar" — incorrect; the correct spelling is "Gangster" (a member of a gang of violent criminals).

NOTE

• Words ending in "-ious" (gregarious, various, curious, serious) are frequently tested for spelling in SSC exams — remember the "i" before "ous".

• Commonly confused endings: "-er" vs "-ar" vs "-or" (gangster, burglar, doctor) — there is no fixed rule, so these must be memorised individually.

question:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.
ABSOLUTE
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. INCOMPLETE.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Absolute" means complete, total, or not qualified or diminished in any way; utter and pure. (पूर्ण/संपूर्ण)
◦ Example: The general demanded absolute obedience from his soldiers.

• The antonym "Incomplete" means not finished or lacking a part, which is the direct opposite of something that is total and entire.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: SHEER — means "absolute, complete, or utter" (e.g. sheer nonsense); it is a synonym, not an antonym, of "absolute".

• Option 2: OUTRIGHT — means "total, complete, unqualified" (e.g. an outright win); it is also a synonym of "absolute".

• Option 4: PURE — means "unmixed, complete, or utter" (e.g. pure luck); it too is close in meaning to "absolute" and hence a synonym, not an antonym.

NOTE

• Words that mean "complete/total": absolute, sheer, outright, utter, entire, total, thorough.

• Their common antonyms: incomplete, partial, qualified, limited — SSC frequently sets synonym-look-alikes as distractors in antonym questions, so always double-check the direction (synonym vs antonym) being asked.

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.
Personal care products can also been made from agricultural ingredients, such as flower or fruit extracts and oils.
option_1: such as flower or fruit extracts and oils.
option_4: also been made from agricultural ingredients,
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. also been made from agricultural ingredients,

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The error lies in the segment "also been made from agricultural ingredients," — the modal "can" must be followed directly by the base form (V1) of the verb, i.e., "be", not the past participle form "been".

• Rule — Modal + Verb: after modal auxiliaries (can, could, may, might, will, shall, should, must), the following verb must always be in its base/first form. For a passive construction it becomes modal + be + V3.
◦ Correct: can also be made (not "can also been made").

• Corrected sentence: "Personal care products can also be made from agricultural ingredients, such as flower or fruit extracts and oils."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "such as flower or fruit extracts and oils." is grammatically correct as it stands; it carries no error.

• Option 2: "Personal care products can" is grammatically correct; the subject and modal are properly used.

• Option 3: "No error" is incorrect because an error does exist, in segment 4.

NOTE

• A very common SSC error-spotting trap is the wrong use of "been" instead of "be" right after a modal verb — always check that modals (can/could/may/might/must/shall/should/will/would) are followed by the bare infinitive.

• Related structures to remember: has/have/had + been + V3 (present/past perfect passive) is correct, but modal + been + V3 (without "have") is always wrong; it must be modal + be + V3.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
Sometimes, even one good ________ can make a big impact on both the person doing it and the person receiving it.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. deed.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Deed" means an action or act, typically one that is performed intentionally or consciously, and is commonly used in the fixed collocation "a good deed".

• The sentence talks about a single kind action affecting both the doer and the receiver — this sense is expressed only by "deed", as in the common phrase "one good deed a day".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "deal" means an agreement or a quantity/transaction (e.g. a business deal, a good deal of money); it does not fit the sense of "a kind action".

• Option 2: "dwell" is a verb meaning to live somewhere or to think/speak at length about something; it cannot be used as a noun after "one good ___".

• Option 3: "drill" means a repetitive training exercise or a tool for boring holes; it is unrelated to the idea of a kind action.

NOTE

• Common fixed collocations with "deed": a good deed, an evil deed, in word and deed.

• Commonly confused word-family: deed (noun: action) vs need (noun: requirement) vs deem (verb: to consider/judge) — SSC often uses such near-homophones as distractors in fill-in-the-blank questions.

question: Choose the incorrectly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. DEBUCHERY.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "DEBAUCHERY", not "DEBUCHERY" — it means excessive indulgence in sensual pleasures; extreme immorality. (व्यभिचार/लंपटता)

• Spelling key: DE + BAUCH + ERY. Note the letters "AU" in the middle syllable, which are missing in the given (incorrect) spelling "DEBUCHERY".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "DUBIOUS" is correctly spelt — meaning hesitating or doubting; not to be relied upon.

• Option 3: "MALIGNANT" is correctly spelt — meaning evil in nature or intent, or (of a tumour) harmful/cancerous.

• Option 4: "CONSCIENCE" is correctly spelt — meaning a person's moral sense of right and wrong.

NOTE

• The word family: debauch (verb), debauchery (noun), debauched (adjective) — all retain the "au" spelling.

• Other words with a silent/tricky "au" combination frequently tested for spelling: gauge, restaurant, applause, dinosaur, exhausted.

question:
Select the word that is closest in meaning (SYNONYM) to the word given below.
Wallow
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Flounder.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Wallow" means to move in a slow, clumsy, ungainly manner, especially by rolling about in mud, water, or a similar substance; to flounder about. (कीचड़ में लोटना/असहाय होकर संघर्ष करना)
◦ Example: The buffaloes were wallowing in the muddy pond to escape the heat.

• "Flounder" shares this core sense of struggling clumsily or moving with difficulty, which makes it the closest synonym among the given options.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Straighten (सीधा करना) means to make or become straight; it is unrelated to clumsy, floundering movement.

• Option 2: Rise (उठना) means to move upward or get up; it is close to an antonym in feel, not a synonym, of "wallow".

• Option 4: Steady (स्थिर करना/करना) means to make or become firm and stable; this is essentially opposite to the unsteady, clumsy sense of "wallow".

NOTE

• "Wallow" also has a figurative sense: to indulge oneself excessively in an unrestrained way in something (e.g. to wallow in self-pity or luxury) — both senses (physical and figurative) involve a lack of restraint or control.

• Related words: welter (to wallow, a near-synonym), grovel (to lie or crawl abjectly), flounder (to struggle helplessly).

question:
Some parts of a paragraph have been jumbled up, and labelled A, B, C and D. Select the option that gives the correct sequence in which these parts can be rearranged to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph.
Carts: carts have two solid wheels.
A. The triangles are distributed in three concentric circles.
B. The wheels are decorated with triangles made of copper.
C. The chassis of the two carts are made of wood and covered with thick copper sheets.
D. The wheels rotated on a fixed axle linked by a shaft to the yoke.
The concentric circles start from the hub flange of the wheel.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. DCBA.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The paragraph must flow logically from the opening line about the carts' wheels to the closing line about concentric circles on the wheel.

• Opening line: "Carts: carts have two solid wheels." connects naturally with D ("The wheels rotated on a fixed axle linked by a shaft to the yoke"), since both sentences continue describing the wheels' mechanism.

◦ C ("The chassis of the two carts are made of wood and covered with thick copper sheets") logically follows next, shifting attention from the wheel mechanism to the body/chassis of the cart.

◦ B ("The wheels are decorated with triangles made of copper") returns the focus to the wheels' decoration, continuing the copper theme introduced in C.

◦ A ("The triangles are distributed in three concentric circles") naturally follows B, elaborating on how the triangles (just mentioned) are arranged.

• This arrangement also correctly leads into the closing line, "The concentric circles start from the hub flange of the wheel," which further explains the "concentric circles" introduced in A.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4 (DCBA).

Additional Information

• Option 1 (BADC) is incorrect because it starts by discussing the triangle decoration (B) before the axle/shaft mechanism (D) has even been introduced, breaking the logical flow from the opening line.

• Option 2 (CBAD) is incorrect because placing D (about the axle) at the end disconnects it from the opening line about the wheels, and does not lead naturally into the closing sentence about concentric circles.

• Option 3 (ABCD) is incorrect because it opens with the concentric-circle detail (A) before the triangles have even been mentioned (which happens only in B), making the reference to "the triangles" in A ungrounded.

NOTE

• In paragraph/jumble questions, always identify the sentence that best continues the topic of the fixed opening line, and separately identify which sentence best leads into the fixed closing line — the correct option must satisfy both ends.

• Watch for definite articles ("the triangles", "the concentric circles") — a sentence using "the" before a noun usually must follow the sentence that first introduces that noun.

question:
Select the word that is closest in meaning (SYNONYM) to the word given below.
Famine
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Drought.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Famine" means an extreme scarcity of food, especially over a wide area, often causing widespread hunger and death. (अकाल/भुखमरी)
◦ Example: The prolonged famine forced thousands of families to migrate in search of food.

• "Drought" refers to a prolonged period of abnormally low rainfall leading to a severe shortage of water and food crops, which is closely linked to and shares the sense of severe scarcity found in "famine" — making it the closest match among the given options.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: Feast (दावत) means a large meal or elaborate celebration involving abundant food — this is the direct opposite of famine.

• Option 3: Abundance (प्रचुरता) means a very large quantity of something, i.e. plentifulness — again the opposite sense of scarcity found in "famine".

• Option 4: Plenty (बहुतायत) means a large or sufficient amount/supply — this too conveys sufficiency, which is the opposite of famine's scarcity.

NOTE

• Word family related to scarcity: famine, dearth, scarcity, shortage, drought, deficiency.

• Their antonyms (abundance-related): plenty, abundance, surplus, profusion, feast — SSC frequently places antonym-like words as distractors in synonym questions, so always check the core sense (scarcity vs abundance) carefully.

question:
Fill in the blank with the most suitable word.
The machine can be ______ to deliver a certain number of coins.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. set.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Set" means to adjust or programme a device/machine to operate in a particular way, as in the common collocation "set to deliver/dispense".

• The sentence describes a machine being adjusted to release a fixed quantity of coins, which is precisely expressed by "set" — e.g. "the alarm is set for 6 a.m." follows the same pattern.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "met" (past participle of "meet") means encountered or satisfied (a requirement); it cannot describe adjusting a machine.

• Option 2: "abet" means to encourage or assist someone in wrongdoing; it is entirely unrelated to configuring a machine.

• Option 3: "slashed" means cut sharply or drastically reduced (e.g. prices slashed); it does not fit the sense of programming a machine.

NOTE

• Common collocations with "set": set a machine/alarm/timer, set a target, set a record, set an example.

• Commonly confused word-family: set (to adjust/fix) vs sit (to be seated) vs seat (to place someone/have capacity for) — these are frequently tested in SSC vocabulary sections.

question:
Choose the word that can substitute the given group of words.
Study of body functions
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Physiology.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Physiology" means the branch of biology dealing with the normal functions of living organisms and their parts, i.e. the study of body functions. (शरीर क्रिया विज्ञान)
◦ Example: The physiology of the human heart is studied in great detail in medical colleges.

• The word is formed from the Greek roots "physio-" (nature/body) + "-logy" (study of), directly matching the given definition "study of body functions".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Genealogy means the study of family lineage/ancestry, not body functions.

• Option 3: Psychology means the scientific study of the human mind and behaviour, not the physical functions of the body.

• Option 4: Astrology means the study of the supposed influence of celestial bodies on human affairs, entirely unrelated to body functions.

NOTE

• Related "-logy" words frequently asked in SSC one-word substitution: Anatomy (study of body structure), Pathology (study of diseases), Physiology (study of body functions), Etymology (study of word origins).

• Do not confuse Physiology (body functions) with Physiognomy (judging character from facial features) — both are common SSC distractors.

question:
Fill in the blank with an appropriate option.
The sun ______ directly in the east and sets directly in the west.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. rises.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Rises" means moves upward, appears above the horizon — the standard verb used for describing the sun's daily appearance in the sky.

• The sentence is completed by the antonym pair "rises...sets", which is the fixed, idiomatic way of describing the sun's daily movement (sunrise in the east, sunset in the west).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "sums" means adds up or totals (as in arithmetic); it makes no sense in the context of the sun's movement.

• Option 3: "expands" means increases in size; the sun does not "expand" daily in the east, it appears/rises.

• Option 4: "elevates" means raises something to a higher position or rank; it is not the natural verb used for the sun's own daily appearance (it is intransitive here, and "elevates" is typically transitive).

NOTE

• Fixed antonym-verb pair frequently tested: the sun rises (in the east) / the sun sets (in the west).

• Related vocabulary: sunrise, sunset, dawn, dusk, twilight — all commonly appear in SSC fill-in-the-blank and vocabulary questions.

question:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Pick the option that gives their correct order.
P. The Spanish flu, also known as the 1918 flu pandemic, was a deadly pandemic in recent history.
Q. It spread worldwide during the year 1918-1919.
R. The virus infected 500 million people – about a third of the world's population at the time.
S. The death toll was estimated to be at least 50 million worldwide, possibly as high as 100 million this makes it the severest pandemic in human history.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. PQRS.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• P must open the paragraph, as it introduces the topic itself: "The Spanish flu, also known as the 1918 flu pandemic, was a deadly pandemic in recent history."

• Q logically follows P, giving the time period of the outbreak: "It spread worldwide during the year 1918-1919" — the pronoun "It" clearly refers back to "The Spanish flu" named in P.

• R follows next, providing the scale of infection: "The virus infected 500 million people..." — continuing chronologically from the spread described in Q.

• S closes the paragraph with the death toll and overall severity: "The death toll was estimated to be at least 50 million worldwide..." — this is the logical concluding statistic after the infection numbers given in R.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1 (PQRS).

Additional Information

• Option 2 (PRSQ) is incorrect because it places R (infection numbers) directly after P, skipping over Q's introduction of the 1918-1919 timeframe, and ends with Q, which reads awkwardly as a conclusion.

• Option 3 (PSRQ) is incorrect because it places S (the death-toll conclusion) too early, before the spread (Q) and infection numbers (R) have even been mentioned.

• Option 4 (SRPQ) is incorrect because it opens with S, the concluding statistic, before the topic (the Spanish flu) has even been introduced by P — the pronoun "this" in S would have no clear antecedent.

NOTE

• In para-jumble questions, the sentence that introduces the proper noun/topic (here, "The Spanish flu") must always come first, and any sentence using a pronoun ("It", "This") must follow the sentence that introduces its antecedent.

• Chronological/logical order (spread → infection scale → death toll) is a strong clue in fact-based paragraphs like this one.

question:
Parts of the following sentence are given as options. Identify the part that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.
And so for the sakes / of his son he remained, / absolutely calm.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. And so for the sakes

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The error lies in the phrase "for the sakes" — the fixed idiomatic expression is "for the sake of", always used with the singular, uncountable noun "sake", never in the plural "sakes".

• Rule — Fixed idiomatic phrase: "for the sake of" (meaning "for the benefit/purpose of") is an invariable expression; "sake" does not take a plural "-s" in this construction.

• Corrected sentence: "And so for the sake of his son he remained, absolutely calm."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "absolutely calm" is grammatically correct; the adverb "absolutely" correctly modifies the adjective "calm".

• Option 2: "No error" is incorrect because an error does exist, in the first segment.

• Option 3: "of his son he remained," is grammatically correct as part of the larger phrase "for the sake of his son he remained".

NOTE

• Other fixed phrases using an invariable singular noun (never pluralised): for God's sake, for heaven's sake, for old times' sake, for the sake of argument.

• SSC frequently tests such "fixed phrase" errors — always check whether a noun inside an idiomatic expression has been wrongly pluralised or singularised.

question:
Choose the option that is the correct indirect form of the sentence.
Ravi said, "I may sell this tie."
option_1: Ravi said that he may sell that tie.
option_2: Ravi said that he might sell that tie.
option_3: Ravi said that I might sell that tie.
option_4: Ravi said that he should sell this tie.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Ravi said that he might sell that tie.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The reporting verb "said" is in the past tense, so standard rules of narration require the necessary backshift of tense, pronoun, and demonstrative changes.

• Rule — Narration change for modal "may": when the reporting verb is in the past tense, "may" changes to "might" in indirect speech.

• Rule — Pronoun and demonstrative change: the first-person pronoun "I" (referring to Ravi) changes to the third-person "he"; the demonstrative pronoun "this" changes to "that" when reporting.
◦ Applying the rules: I → he; may → might; this tie → that tie.
◦ Indirect: Ravi said that he might sell that tie.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because "may" has not been changed to "might", which is mandatory when the reporting verb is in the past tense.

• Option 3 is incorrect because the pronoun "I" has not been converted to the third person "he", even though the reported speaker (Ravi) is referred to in the third person.

• Option 4 is incorrect because "should" is the wrong modal here — "may" changes only to "might" in narration, and using "should" also alters the original meaning (possibility vs. obligation); it also wrongly retains "this" instead of changing it to "that".

NOTE

• Modal changes in narration: can → could, may → might, will → would, must → had to/must.

• Place/time and demonstrative changes: this → that, these → those, here → there, now → then, today → that day, tomorrow → the next day, yesterday → the day before.

question:
Fill in the blank with an appropriate option.
A group of Googlers get together regularly to ______ and decide which events will be celebrated with a doodle.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. brainstorm.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Brainstorm" means to hold a group discussion to produce ideas or solve a problem by collectively generating and evaluating ideas.

• The sentence describes a group of people meeting regularly to discuss and decide on ideas (which events to celebrate), which is exactly the sense conveyed by "brainstorm".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "discredit" means to harm the reputation of someone or cast doubt on something; it does not fit a context of collaborative idea generation.

• Option 3: "relief" is a noun meaning a feeling of reassurance/relaxation after anxiety, or aid given to those in need; it cannot grammatically or logically fill this verb slot.

• Option 4: "salute" means to greet or acknowledge with a formal gesture of respect; it is unrelated to group discussion of ideas.

NOTE

• Common collocations with "brainstorm": to brainstorm ideas, a brainstorming session, to brainstorm solutions.

• Related vocabulary for group idea-generation: deliberate, confer, collaborate, strategize.

question:
Choose the word that means the same as the given word.
Lair
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Concealment.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Lair" means a wild animal's den or resting place; more broadly, a hidden place where a person goes to be alone or to hide. (गुफा/छिपने का स्थान)
◦ Example: The fugitive was finally traced to his secret lair in the hills.

• "Concealment" shares this core sense of being hidden or kept out of sight, making it the closest match in meaning to "lair" among the given options.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: Arraign (अभियोग लगाना) means to call or bring someone before a court to answer a criminal charge; it has no connection to a hiding place.

• Option 3: Apart (अलग) means separated by distance, or aside from; it does not convey the idea of a hidden den.

• Option 4: Concurrent (समवर्ती) means existing or happening at the same time; it is unrelated in meaning to "lair".

NOTE

• Related "hiding place" vocabulary: den, hideout, hideaway, retreat, burrow, refuge.

• "Lair" is also used figuratively for a person's private retreat, e.g., "his study was his lair" — SSC often tests such extended/figurative senses of concrete nouns.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
To the manner born
option_2: To do something as though it is coming naturally
option_4: To give a ride to someone
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. To do something as though it is coming naturally.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "To the manner born" means to be entirely suited to a particular role, way of life, or activity from birth, so that one does it naturally and with ease, as though born to it. (जन्मजात रूप से किसी कार्य के अनुकूल होना)
◦ Example: She took to public speaking as though to the manner born, never once appearing nervous.

• The phrase originates from Shakespeare's Hamlet, where it originally referred to being accustomed to a custom from birth; today it is used for natural ease or aptitude in any activity.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: To have high manners — this wrongly takes "manner" literally as "good manners/etiquette", which is not the idiomatic sense.

• Option 3: To be sophisticated — describes refinement or worldly polish, which is not what this idiom conveys; it is about natural ease, not sophistication.

• Option 4: To give a ride to someone — this confuses "manner" with an unrelated idea entirely disconnected from the idiom's actual meaning.

NOTE

• Note the frequently misspelled/confused word pair in this idiom: "manner" (way of doing something) here, not "manor" (a large country house) — SSC sometimes tests this distinction separately.

• Other idioms of natural aptitude: "a born leader", "second nature" (something done so often it feels automatic), "in one's element" (comfortable doing what one is good at).

question:
Comprehension:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Krishna helped my husbands create a strategy. They (1) ________ by killing Jarasandha, the most feared (2) ________ of the time—and incidentally, a long time enemy of Krishna. (3) ________ released the many kings Jarasandha had imprisoned in his labyrinths and gave them back (4) ________ kingdoms. This made my husband so popular that (5) ________ they went after that, they were greeted with friendship.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. began.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage is narrated entirely in the Simple Past Tense ("helped", "released", "gave", "made", "went", "were greeted"), so the verb filling blank (1) must also be in the simple past form.

• Rule — Simple Past Tense: the simple past of the irregular verb "begin" is "began" (begin – began – begun); "began" is used directly as a finite main verb, without any auxiliary.
◦ "They began by killing Jarasandha..." — correctly continues the past-tense narration of the passage.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "commence" is the base/present form of the verb ("to commence"); it does not match the required simple past tense.

• Option 2: "begun" is the past participle (V3) of "begin", which requires an auxiliary verb ("had begun"/"have begun") to be grammatically correct — it cannot stand alone as a simple past finite verb.

• Option 4: "initiate" is also a base/present form verb, and additionally is not the correct paradigm word being tested (begin/began/begun) for this blank.

NOTE

• Irregular verb forms often confused in cloze passages: begin – began – begun, go – went – gone, do – did – done — the simple past (2nd form) is used alone, while the past participle (3rd form) always needs an auxiliary.

• Always check the overriding tense of the whole passage before choosing the verb form for any individual blank.

question:
Comprehension:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Krishna helped my husbands create a strategy. They (1) ________ by killing Jarasandha, the most feared (2) ________ of the time—and incidentally, a long time enemy of Krishna. (3) ________ released the many kings Jarasandha had imprisoned in his labyrinths and gave them back (4) ________ kingdoms. This made my husband so popular that (5) ________ they went after that, they were greeted with friendship.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. ruler.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank follows the adjective phrase "the most feared" and is itself followed by "of the time", so a person-noun is grammatically required to complete the phrase "the most feared ___ of the time" — describing what Jarasandha was.

• "Ruler" (a person who rules, e.g. a king) fits this slot perfectly: "the most feared ruler of the time" correctly describes Jarasandha as a widely-feared king.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "dominion" is an abstract noun meaning "the power or right to govern" or "a territory ruled over"; it cannot describe a person and does not fit "the most feared ___".

• Option 3: "rule" is either a verb or an abstract noun meaning "government/authority"; like "dominion", it is not a person-noun and cannot be "feared" the way a person can.

• Option 4: "sovereignty" is an abstract noun meaning "supreme power or authority"; again, it denotes a concept, not a person, and cannot correctly complete "the most feared ___ of the time".

NOTE

• Distinguish person-nouns from abstract nouns in the same word family: ruler (person) vs. rule/dominion/sovereignty (abstract concepts of authority).

• Cloze passages frequently test exactly this kind of part-of-speech/sense discrimination — always check whether the blank needs a person, a thing, or an abstract quality based on the surrounding words.

question:
Comprehension:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Krishna helped my husbands create a strategy. They (1) ________ by killing Jarasandha, the most feared (2) ________ of the time—and incidentally, a long time enemy of Krishna. (3) ________ released the many kings Jarasandha had imprisoned in his labyrinths and gave them back (4) ________ kingdoms. This made my husband so popular that (5) ________ they went after that, they were greeted with friendship.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. They then.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank begins a new sentence: **"(3) ________ released the many kings Jarasandha had imprisoned..." — it therefore needs a subject ("They", referring back to "my husbands"/Krishna and the Pandavas) followed by a sequencing adverb** showing the next step in the narrative.

• "They then" correctly supplies the subject "They" plus the time-sequence adverb "then" (meaning "next, after that"), giving a grammatically complete and logical sentence: "They then released the many kings..."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "Their after they" is grammatically nonsensical — "Their" is a possessive adjective that needs a noun after it, and "after they" is an incomplete subordinate clause; the combination does not form a valid subject for the sentence.

• Option 3: "They kept" wrongly introduces the verb "kept" before the actual main verb "released" of the sentence, producing a double-verb error ("They kept released the many kings...").

• Option 4: "Then after they" is grammatically incomplete and awkward — it strings together two time-connectors without a proper subject-verb structure to open the sentence correctly.

NOTE

• When a cloze blank starts a new sentence, always check first whether a subject is needed, and then whether any additional adverb/connector is needed — the correct option must produce a complete, standalone grammatical sentence.

• Sequencing adverbs such as "then", "next", "after that", "subsequently" are common cloze-test items testing logical narrative flow.

question:
Comprehension:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Krishna helped my husbands create a strategy. They (1) ________ by killing Jarasandha, the most feared (2) ________ of the time—and incidentally, a long time enemy of Krishna. (3) ________ released the many kings Jarasandha had imprisoned in his labyrinths and gave them back (4) ________ kingdoms. This made my husband so popular that (5) ________ they went after that, they were greeted with friendship.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. their.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank appears in **"gave them back (4) ________ kingdoms", which requires a possessive adjective agreeing with the plural noun "them"** (referring to "the many kings") to show that the kingdoms belonged to those kings.

• "Their" is the correct possessive adjective for a plural antecedent ("the many kings"), correctly conveying: "gave them back their [own] kingdoms."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "whose" is a possessive relative pronoun used to introduce a relative clause (e.g. "the kings whose kingdoms..."); it cannot be used here since no relative clause is being formed at this point in the sentence.

• Option 3: "there" is an adverb of place ("in/at that place") and is not a possessive form at all; it cannot logically precede the noun "kingdoms" to show ownership.

• Option 4: "that" is a demonstrative/relative pronoun, not a possessive adjective; "gave them back that kingdoms" is grammatically incorrect since "that" would need to agree with a singular noun and cannot show possession here.

NOTE

• Commonly confused homophones/near-homophones in cloze tests: their (possessive) vs. there (place) vs. they're (they are).

• Possessive adjectives must always agree in number/person with the noun they refer back to: their (plural), his/her/its (singular), your, our, my.

question:
Comprehension:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Krishna helped my husbands create a strategy. They (1) ________ by killing Jarasandha, the most feared (2) ________ of the time—and incidentally, a long time enemy of Krishna. (3) ________ released the many kings Jarasandha had imprisoned in his labyrinths and gave them back (4) ________ kingdoms. This made my husband so popular that (5) ________ they went after that, they were greeted with friendship.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. wherever.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank appears in **"so popular that (5) ________ they went after that, they were greeted with friendship" — the sense required is that no matter which place** they travelled to, they received a friendly welcome, i.e. a place-based "no matter where" meaning.

• "Wherever" is the compound relative adverb meaning "at, in, or to whatever place", correctly completing the sense: "wherever they went...they were greeted with friendship."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "if at all" means "if it happens at all/to any extent"; it does not carry the place-related "no matter where" sense required by "...they went...".

• Option 2: "whichever" means "no matter which one (of a set of choices)", used typically with a noun (e.g. "whichever kingdom"); it does not fit naturally before "they went", which needs a place-adverb, not a choice-selector.

• Option 3: "when if" is not a standard English conjunction/adverb combination at all and produces an ungrammatical sentence.

NOTE

• Compound relative adverbs frequently tested in cloze passages: wherever (place), whenever (time), however (manner/degree), whoever (person), whichever (choice).

• The clue word "went" (a verb of motion to a place) is a strong signal that the blank needs a place-related connector like "wherever".
